products.name: Gamakay TK75HE V2 Hall Effect Keyboard, 75%, Phoenix V3 silent magnetic switches, wired / 2.4 GHz / Bluetooth
specs: Phoenix V3 silent linear magnetic or Mercury V3 linear magnetic, hot-swappable
Rapid trigger, Snap Tap, DKS, per-key actuation
Small screen for settings and GIFs
products.warranty: 1 year on the keyboard from the order date (battery 3 months), per Gamakay's policy
products.returns: 14 days from delivery; must be unused in its original packaging, with return authorization; buyer pays return shipping; opened working items may carry a 35% restocking fee
products.summary: The cheapest well-reviewed wireless keyboard that ships with silent magnetic switches. Reviewers describe a soft thunk rather than a clack.
products.fit: Windows gamers who want rapid trigger without waking a roommate, on a budget under $100.
caveats: Gamakay's driver never detected it on a Mac in AppleInsider's test, so Mac users can't tune actuation.
Plastic case that picks up finger oil; PC Gamer and AppleInsider both call the build weak.
The 2.4 GHz dongle falls out of its holder when the rear feet are open.
Battery capacity isn't listed on the maker pages we read.
Ships from Gamakay's US warehouse: 1-3 days handling plus 9-12 days transit, $3.50 standard shipping.

products.name: Gamakay TK75 TMR Magnetic Keyboard, 75%, Phoenix V3 silent switches, 8,000 mAh, takes magnetic or mechanical switches
specs: Phoenix V3 silent or Mercury V3 magnetic; also accepts 5-pin mechanical switches
8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz, 1,000 Hz Bluetooth (HLPlanet)
Rapid trigger, SOCD / Snap Tap, per-key actuation
products.warranty: 1 year on the keyboard from the order date (battery 3 months), per Gamakay's policy
products.returns: 14 days from delivery; must be unused in its original packaging, with return authorization; buyer pays return shipping; opened working items may carry a 35% restocking fee
products.summary: Same silent Phoenix V3 switches as the TK75HE V2, with an 8,000 mAh battery and a TMR board that also takes silent mechanical switches.
products.fit: People who use it wireless all day, or who want to mix silent mechanical switches with magnetic ones.
caveats: Smartzone measured 4-7 days at 8 hours a day with the screen and RGB on; up to 20 days with both off.
Plate flex can cause phantom releases with rapid trigger below about 0.3 mm; HLPlanet suggests 0.4 mm.
Turn rapid trigger off on any key fitted with a mechanical switch, or it can double-type.
The software is English only and less polished than Wooting's (HLPlanet, Smartzone).
Gamakay's 12% Awin code excludes this model.

specs: Phoenix V3 silent or White Jade magnetic, hot-swappable
Rapid trigger, Snap Tap, adjustable dead zone 0-1 mm
products.warranty: 1 year on the keyboard from the order date (battery 3 months), per Gamakay's policy
products.returns: 14 days from delivery; must be unused in its original packaging, with return authorization; buyer pays return shipping; opened working items may carry a 35% restocking fee
products.summary: Gamakay's lowest-priced 75% board with the Phoenix V3 silent switch option, plus a big knob and gasket mount.
products.fit: Shoppers who want the lowest price for a silent magnetic board and like a volume knob.
caveats: Pick the Phoenix V3 switch option; the White Jade option isn't sold as silent.
Battery capacity isn't listed on the maker pages we read.
Few independent reviews yet; one buyer comment on Gamakay's site reports wired mode not being recognized.
Ships from Gamakay's US warehouse in about 10-15 days.

notes: QUERY: 'silent hall effect keyboard'. Google autocomplete suggests it, along with 'quiet hall effect keyboard', 'silent hall effect gaming keyboard' and the 'reddit' variants. Current results are thin: Gamakay's and Gateron's own blogs, Epomaker's store page, a hobby blog and switch listings, with no real comparison page. PAIN POINTS (Reddit was not reachable; counts come from reviews and listings): software confusing, half-baked or broken on Mac, 6 of 6 reviews (TechRadar headline, PC Gamer snippet, Notebookcheck, HLPlanet TMR, Smartzone, AppleInsider); plastic or weak build, 3 (PC Gamer, AppleInsider, HLPlanet); dongle falls out with the feet open, 2 (AppleInsider, Smartzone); phantom releases or self-triggering at low rapid-trigger settings, 2 (HLPlanet TMR, Gamakay TMR blog); switch compatibility limits on silent switches, 4 (HLPlanet, Lumekeebs, Keychron page, DrunkDeer/Raesha); stabilizer ticking, 1 (Notebookcheck, on the mechanical TK75 V2); moderate battery with screen and RGB on, 1 (Smartzone); Mac software failure, 1 (AppleInsider, 2.5/5). On noise, AppleInsider, HLPlanet (twice), Smartzone and a hobby blog call the Phoenix switches quiet. Tom's Guide (original TK75 HE, V1 Phoenix) reportedly called them clacky; that came from a search snippet only, so it is left off the page. SEGMENTS AND WINNERS: (1) budget quiet gaming on Windows: Gamakay TK75HE V2, the most-reviewed board shipping silent magnetic switches, and HLPlanet calls Gamakay essentially the only mainstream silent magnetic option; (2) lowest price or a knob: Gamakay NS75; (3) all-day wireless or mixing in mechanical switches: Gamakay TK75 TMR (8,000 mAh; 8 kHz on 2.4 GHz per HLPlanet); (4) Mac: Keychron K2 HE ($129.99 on keychron.com 2026-11-11; not silent; no program, so a maker link only); (5) best software and DIY silent: Wooting plus Gateron Magnetic Jade Silent (Divinikey $14.22 per 18, 2026-11-11). VERIFIED 2026-11-11 on gamakay.com: TK75HE V2 variants all $89.99 (ANSI, ISO DE, ISO UK; black or white; Phoenix V3 or Mercury V3; ISO UK black out of stock) via storecheck product. NS75 $79.99 and TK75 TMR $109.99, both available, came from the store's search JSON. The storecheck product endpoint and WebFetch returned HTTP 429 for NS75 and TMR all session, so their variant lists were not read. Shipping and returns come from the policy pages. The homepage prints no code; its banners are '12%OFF' on NS75 and 'Sign up and get 11% OFF'. The TK68 title carries code TK68PD, but TK68 is not recorded here, so it is left out of codes. UNVERIFIED, kept off the page: TK75HE V2 battery (keeb-finder says 4,000 mAh) and its per-mode polling; NS75 battery, default switch and wireless polling; Phoenix V3 actuation force (HLPlanet 45 ± 5 gf vs PC Gamer 40 g); DrunkDeer A75 Pro / G75 silent-switch option and price (drunkdeer.com failed with a certificate error; snippets say $127.99-$139.99, wired); Wooting 80HE+ price (pre-order, 'similar to 80HE'); whether Wooting 80HE+ accepts Phoenix V3 (HLPlanet confirms Wooting 60HE only). AMAZON: amzcheck is walled, so no Amazon records. AppleInsider (March 2026) saw the TK75HE V2 at $77.39 on Amazon vs $79.20 on gamakay.com with GK12. Today's Amazon price could not be checked, so we link the maker via Awin. The PC Gamer and TechRadar review bodies were blocked; only their headlines and snippets were read.
